name: Lower Ideal of a Convex Geometry
statement: A finite convex geometry on $E$ is an intersection-closed family $\mathcal G\subseteq2^E$ containing $\varnothing$ and $E$, in which every proper member can gain one element and remain in $\mathcal G$. A nonempty subfamily $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal G$ is a lower ideal when $Y\in\mathcal I$, $X\in\mathcal G$, and $X\subseteq Y$ imply $X\in\mathcal I$. Up to coordinate reflections and suppression of constants, the one-inclusion graphs of these ideals form $\mathsf{Icg}$.
hypotheses: Finite ground set and nonempty ideal.
